findings.title: Anchor validation requires anchors in English order and rejects legitimate reordering
findings.body: santizeAnchors() advances the translation matcher and the English matcher in lock-step and requires matcher.group() to equal the next English anchor. A translation that legitimately reorders two different links relative to English (common when word order differs between languages) therefore reports 'Didn't find anchor tag' on the first anchor and breaks, even though both anchors are present unchanged. The check should compare the anchors as a multiset/set rather than requiring identical order.

findings.title: Anchor pattern also matches unrelated tags starting with 'a'
findings.body: ANCHOR_PATTERN is '</?a[^>]*>' with no word boundary or tag-name terminator, so it matches <abbr>, <address>, <article>, <aside> and any other a-prefixed tag, not just <a>. Such tags in a translation are either falsely reported as missing anchors, or, if the same a-prefixed tag exists in English, are stripped by santizeAnchors() and thereby whitelisted past the OWASP check regardless of their attributes. The pattern should be something like '</?a(\\s[^>]*)?>'.

findings.title: Missing English bundle aborts verification with RuntimeException instead of reporting a problem
findings.body: If the derived *_en.properties file does not exist (a new locale/theme, or a properties file whose path does not match the resources-community/resources and locale-suffix rewriting), verifySafeHtml() throws an unchecked RuntimeException. verify() only documents/declares MojoExecutionException and its callers expect a List<String> of problems, so one missing English file aborts the whole verification run and hides all other findings for all files instead of producing a per-file message.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 was changed from the Lithuanian FreeOTP/Google Authenticator text to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the anchor removal should have kept a Lithuanian sentence such as the generic 'install one of the following applications on your mobile' wording in Lithuanian.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 was changed from the Lithuanian FreeOTP/Google Authenticator text to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian. Lithuanian users will see instructions in the wrong language; the anchor removal should have kept a Lithuanian sentence such as the generic 'install one of the following applications on your mobile' wording in Lithuanian.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file now uses Traditional Chinese characters for totpStep1
findings.body: messages_zh_CN.properties is the Simplified Chinese bundle, but the replacement totpStep1 uses Traditional forms (手機/安裝/應用程式 instead of 手机/安装/应用程序). Simplified Chinese users will see text in the wrong script; the replacement should use Simplified Chinese characters.

findings.title: No test that legitimate HTML passes verification cleanly
findings.body:
All new tests assert only that a problem message is present (hasItem 'Illegal HTML' / 'Didn't find anchor tag'); there is no fixture asserting an empty result for a valid translation, e.g. one that copies the English

//
markup or reuses the identical anchor from English. A regression that flags every value (wrong policy, wrong
normalization, wrong English-file derivation) would still pass the whole suite.
